Let’s dive into Chapter 1: Why Intuition Fails in Modern Business.
You’ve probably noticed how often people celebrate trusting their gut in business. We hear stories about leaders who made bold moves thanks to a hunch, and movies love to paint this picture of instinctive genius.
But here’s the thing—behind all that glamour is a much different story. Our intuition, which helped our ancestors survive in a much simpler world, just isn’t built for the complicated, high-stakes choices businesses face today.
Think about it. Human intuition evolved to help small groups deal with immediate threats—like spotting a predator in the bushes, or figuring out if someone’s friendly or dangerous. These instincts work fast and almost automatically, great for quick decisions in familiar situations.
But let’s be honest—the modern business world is nothing like the wild. Today’s decisions are filled with uncertainty, tons of abstract data, and long-term consequences. Our brains aren’t naturally wired to handle all that.
Imagine you’re a manager making a hiring decision. The candidate seems friendly, confident, and you just click with them. Your gut says, “This is the one.” But what’s really going on? That feeling is often shaped by subconscious biases—maybe you’re drawn to people who remind you of yourself, rather than those who are actually the best fit. And if that new hire doesn’t work out, the cost of a bad call can be huge.
Here’s something important to remember: this isn’t a personal flaw. It’s something we all deal with. Our brains use shortcuts, called heuristics, to help us make quick choices. These shortcuts are helpful for simple, everyday decisions, but they often lead us astray when things get complicated or unfamiliar.
It’s easy to see why intuition is so tempting. It feels natural, effortless—like second nature. But relying on gut feelings in business? Well, it’s a bit like trying to use a compass made for the North Pole to find your way through a city’s subway system. The tool is real, but the environment has changed.
So, how do we get past this trap? The first step is realizing that intuition has its limits, and understanding why it often lets us down. This kind of awareness is what opens the door to a better way of making decisions—one that leans on evidence, reflection, and a clear look at how our minds really work.
